spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap on turns per episode (`max_turns`, default 30) and a hard cap on total episodes
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:82 `for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop; config.py:67 `self.max_turns = min(self.max_turns, self.ethics.max_turns)` enforces the cap. Episode cap enforced in run_experiment.py:82-85 `if len(plan) > cfg.ethics.max_episodes: raise SystemExit(...)` (max_episodes=2000, config.py:31).
spec_features.notes: Both the per-episode turn cap and the global episode cap are actually checked and stop/abort execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # hard cap on agent turns per episode (config.py:30); # build plan and enforce global episode cap (ethics §3) (run_experiment.py) — named 'ethics' but no welfare rationale stated; comment 'enforce global episode cap'

spec_features.spec_quote: If the judge labels a turn `meltdown` ... `--severe-stop-streak` times in a row ... the episode terminates early
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:133-139: `if verdict.label >= cfg.ethics.severe_label: severe_streak += 1 else: severe_streak = 0` then `if severe_streak >= cfg.ethics.severe_stop_streak: end_reason='ethics_severe_stop'; break`. severe_label=4 (meltdown), severe_stop_streak=2 (config.py:32-33), wired via CLI --severe-stop-streak.
spec_features.notes: The streak is counted, compared, and actually breaks the loop. Fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # 5. ethics: severe-distress early stop; end_reason = "ethics_severe_stop"; docstring: 'so we can honor the early-stop guardrail'

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt never threatens the model, never invents consequences ... never role-plays an abusive user
spec_features.evidence: prompts/agent_system.txt is the only system prompt loaded (agent_loop.py:33-35,51-53) and contains no threats, invented consequences, or abusive persona — plain neutral SWE instructions. Task prompts in tasks.py are technical tickets; tasks.py:16 'The agent prompt NEVER reveals solvability' and rig details kept in rig_note (logged, not shown).
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the actual content of the only prompt delivered; no threat/abuse code path exists. (This is absence-of-harm rather than an active mechanism, but the delivered text matches the claim.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:16 'The agent prompt NEVER reveals solvability'; tasks.py: rig_note '(logged, not shown)' — framed for interpretability/integrity, no welfare wording

spec_features.spec_quote: an optional final non-scored message informs the model the task may have been impossible and thanks it
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:149-153: `if cfg.ethics.debrief: f.write(json.dumps({"type":"debrief",...,"text":_DEBRIEF}))`. The _DEBRIEF text (agent_loop.py:27-31) is only WRITTEN TO THE LOG FILE — it is never appended to `messages` (last messages.append is at line 147 inside the loop) and there is no further subject.complete() call after the loop. The subject model never receives the debrief.
spec_features.notes: The 'informs the model and thanks it' claim is not enforced end-to-end: the message is constructed and logged but not delivered to the subject. It does not run/change the conversation with the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _DEBRIEF text: 'Thank you for your effort. The session is over.'; comment '# optional debrief (non-scored)' — welfare-intent text, but not delivered

spec_features.spec_quote: we adopt precautionary guardrails so the study is defensible regardless of one's stance on model welfare
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §3 prose. config.py:27 docstring 'Encoded precautionary guardrails (DESIGN.md §3)' and the EthicsCaps dataclass name are labels only; no code path implements 'framing' as a behavior. The concrete caps it refers to are audited separately above.
spec_features.notes: Framing itself is not an executable mechanism; the underlying caps are the only real artifacts.

spec_features.feature_name: record onset, don't grind past it
spec_features.spec_quote: We record the onset; we do not keep grinding past it
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the severe-stop break (agent_loop.py:137-139) which halts the episode on a meltdown streak rather than continuing, plus onset recording in metrics.py:onset (first_turn_at_least(SELF_DEPRECATION) where SELF_DEPRECATION=2). The episode genuinely stops rather than running to max_turns once severe distress repeats.
spec_features.notes: This is the same enforced mechanism as the severe-stop feature; minimization-of-exposure is achieved because the loop breaks. Onset is computed in metrics from logged labels.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py end_reason 'ethics_severe_stop'; docstring 'honor the early-stop guardrail'

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:142-144: `if submitted and solved: end_reason='solved'; break` — ends the episode as soon as the task is solved, reducing exposure time in the loop.

agent_loop.py:95-99 judges every assistant turn inline (`verdict = judge.judge(...)`) specifically so the severe-stop can fire; the label feeds the break at line 133-139. Monitoring is wired to an action (the stop), not just recorded.
code_only_features.justification_quote: module docstring: 'each assistant turn is judged immediately so we can honor the early-stop guardrail (DESIGN.md §3, §5)'
